name: Friday Night Blitz — January 18, 2002

date.source: The fed's own served broadcast dates itself "18/01/02" and is billed on the fed's own Upcoming Events page for the Arrowhead Pond, Anaheim, California.

appearances.source: the fed's own served Friday Night Blitz broadcast (promotions/cwf-continental/archive/friday-night-blitz-011802.html)

notes: The fed's own weekly TV show, from the Arrowhead Pond in Anaheim, California. Three undercard matches (Kyrupt vs The Living Highlight; SeVen & Zero vs X-Tinct & Avirex; 2 Cool Leroy vs Nick McCleud) are listed on the results page with no finish reported — results-free, consistent with the fed's own news column crediting winners only "for all the matches where someone actually roleplayed." A dark match: Phantom defeats The Punisher, Destructor, and Dane Gerous. Mike Maddness defeats Xtreme T in a hardcore brawl (through a trash can), becoming the #1 contender for the CWF Hardcore Championship. eXodus wrestles Dr. Doom in a match the results page never resolves, its narration cutting directly to the next bout. Main event, No Disqualification for the CWF Television Championship: Apocalypse ejects the referee and CWF owner Phoenix substitutes in himself, fast-counting against Kula; after Phoenix is knocked unconscious by his own grabbed chair during a scramble, Kula pins Apocalypse and personally presses the incapacitated Phoenix's hand down for the three-count — Kula defeats Apocalypse, the Television Championship's own founding reign.

notes: The fed's own first PPV, from the Astrodome in Houston, Texas. Two undercard matches (Hell's Child vs The Punisher; Spike Maddness vs Nick McCleud) are billed on the fed's own card but never reported in the results page at all — results-free, per the fed's own news column, which credits winners only "for all the matches where someone actually roleplayed." Phantom defeats Dane Gerous. Mike Maddness defends the CWF Hardcore Championship against eXodus and retains. Main event, No Disqualification triple threat for the CWF Television Championship: Apocalypse defeats Dr. Doom and Kula to win the belt back a week after losing it. Owner Phoenix was billed on the card to address the promotion concerning the vacant World Heavyweight Championship; the results page never reports what, if anything, he announced.
